versions.changelog: Security: artifact is SKILL.md only, scope section first (owned accounts, human review, stop on platform defenses, AI disclosure), timezone placeholder.

v1.0.2 — SKILL.md et README.md strictement identiques a la 1.0.1 (SHA-256 verifie). Cette version ne corrige que des canaux de release.

13 dist-tags crees par erreur restaient figes sur la 1.0.0, servant le contenu anterieur a la reecriture de doctrine. Ils pointent desormais tous vers le contenu courant.

skill-card.md n'est pas repris: le CLI le traite comme un artefact generable et le retire a chaque publication (stripGeneratedSkillCards). L'ancienne carte decrivait encore la doctrine pre-reecriture.

Les dist-tags ne sont pas supprimables (ni CLI, ni API, ni interface web); les repointer est le seul levier disponible.

v1.1.0 — Non-breaking additions on top of the v1.0.0 doctrine.

Added:
- Quick config (YAML) block in Section 0 — drop-in config.yaml for agents, including a schedule.windows block for cron timing.
- Compatibility table in Section 0 — install paths for Claude Code, OpenClaw, ClawHub, Cursor / Copilot CLI, and generic LLM agents.
- Section 7 — First-run checklist (7 items before enabling any cron) + a bash one-liner to init memory files.
- Section 8 — Reply skeletons: 3 drop-in templates (Answer-first, Empathy + redirect, Polite correction) with "what to never paste verbatim" guardrails.
- Section 9 — FAQ (OpenClaw requirement, multi-account, X API rate limits, threads vs single tweets, X Premium/Blue, suspension handling).
- init-memory.sh shipped with the companion GitHub repo (idempotent memory-dir bootstrap).

Unchanged: Sections 1-6 (the core doctrine) are byte-identical to v1.0.0. Existing crons keep working without modification.

Full changelog: https://github.com/AlexBloch-IA/twitter-account-operations/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md

Initial release.

- Three-role mental model (post / engage / stealth) for any X account.
- Human-like browser discipline: right page first, let UI load, read before clicking.
- Full cron-by-cron playbook: notifications, keyword monitor (morning/midday/evening),
  reply pass, original posts (morning/noon/evening), thread generator, result
  publish, daily metrics recap.
- Strict reply qualification — no impulse posting, no generic CTAs.
- Recovery playbook for every common failure mode (browser down, frozen, composer
  stuck, page unusable).
- Explicit anti-patterns to avoid.
